dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. I wanted to ask whether there was a space around here dedicated to training?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I wouldn't want to disturb anyone during my shooting practice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm not picky about my surroundings.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: How noisy or crowded a place might be... Those factors are inconsequential. I'm not easily affected by my external environment.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Most importantly... I've found no threats to our survival in this place. You've done well.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Think nothing of it. I should be the one thanking you for keeping this place so safe.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: In any case, thank you for inviting me to this place.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I'll be staying here for a little longer. I hope my being here doesn't inconvenience you.

choices.text: We are in The Realm Within, after all.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Its mechanical principles and aesthetic design are both quite commendable. This place is truly eye-opening.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Ah, that's entirely up to you. Different people have different senses of humor. I don't know what you find amusing, so it wouldn't be appropriate for me to give you an answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Of course. Anything you want to talk about?

choices.text: How about a story from before you became a Champion Duelist?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Well, before I met Navia...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, you're going that far back!?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: You wanted to hear a story from before I became a duelist, correct? I see no harm in starting there.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Anyway, before I met Navia, I lived with my Master. She was a powerful and strict woman who had a big impact on many parts of my childhood.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I was once terrified of monsters that are active at night. I felt like I could never predict or anticipate their attacks.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: So, Master tied a piece of cloth around my eyes, pushed me into the woods, and announced that I was surrounded by a horde of monsters. She did this to teach me to react and respond to them with only sound and instinct as my guide.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I used to be afraid of being alone. I could never fall asleep without her by my side.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: So, for quite some time, she forced me to train every day until I felt like I could no longer lift my arms. Only then would she allow me to rest.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: As a result, seeing her face after I woke up soon turned into a nightmare rather than a comfort...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Before I knew it, I had become as tough as her.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Were I to take on my own apprentice, I'm not sure I could think of a better way to train them, and that thought scares me most of all.

choices.text: What about a fun tidbit from your work as a Champion Duelist?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: My work as a Champion Duelist... Hmm.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: In my profession, "work" and "fun" are two elements that rarely converge.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I've heard many colleagues describe how, on their way home from work, they're often dragged into cafés by their soon-to-be opponents and forced to listen to an endless list of grievances.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: What a waste of time... I'm very thankful something like that has never happened to me.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I wouldn't go asking around for stories about our line of work.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: The profession of a duelist may seem dramatic and full of unexpected twists, but, in most circumstances, it's usually the result of hypocrisy and dark human desires... the type of stories that will only leave you disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Hmm... How about a game inspired by the practice of duels?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you tell me how to play first...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: It's pretty simple. We'll use the Fateometer to determine the rules of the duel and the weapons we can use. I used to play this a lot with my Master. Although, back then, we just rolled a die.

choices.text: What if you roll a "critical failure"...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Then, unfortunately, you have to fight with your hands and feet tied.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aren't duels supposed to be fair?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Of course, but that only applies to duels held before a court of law to defend someone's honor. The duels in this game are meant to improve a Marechaussee Hunter's ability to survive in the wild.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: As a Hunter, there are times when your arm or leg might be out of commission due to injury. But, you have to be able to keep fighting.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: "Never stop thinking about how to secure victory" — that's what my Master taught me.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Once, after two very unlucky rolls, she was forced to fight with a small tree branch as her only weapon. In the end, I still lost.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: In any case, the randomness of it all can really help you test your limits. If you lose, just start over and roll again.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: So, what do you think? Ready to play a round?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Sure! Bring it on!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Hmm, the look of determination in your eyes says more than you know. I like it.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Let's begin. The loser owes the winner a meal.

choices.text: What if you roll a "critical success"...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Then, congratulations, you get to use the weapon of your choice and negate one lethal hit. Your opponent would have to land two hits on you to win.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aren't duels supposed to be fair?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Of course, but that only applies to duels held before a court of law to defend someone's honor. The duels in this game are meant to improve a Marechaussee Hunter's ability to survive in the wild.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Even with preparation and luck on your side, get too confident, and even the greatest of Hunters can still suffer defeat.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: A "critical success" can often be what leads to a "critical failure."

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: My luck is pretty good, so I've had my fair share of good rolls in these games. Even so, when I fought against Master, I often lost in the moments when I was most assured of victory.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: "Prey is most easily caught when it believes itself invincible" — that's what my Master taught me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Clorinde.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Good morning. I hope you find success in your endeavors today.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Clorinde.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Good night. I hope you're able to get some good rest. This place appears quite safe, so I don't think I'll need to keep watch tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Now that I think of it, the Maison Cardinalice set up an archive room to store information related to duels.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: A complete case file would include the cause of the duel, the verdict rendered, the persons and duelists involved, and of course, the final outcome of the duel.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I've never felt the need to look up anything there myself. I believe all my duelist colleagues feel the same way. It's best to leave the recordkeeping to the Gestionnaires — they seem to actually enjoy that kind of work.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In my younger years, I learned a fair amount about botany.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: As a result, I can now differentiate between edible and non-edible roots, identify poisonous fruits... and create simple dyes from the things I forage.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Hmm, the plants in this flower bed are harmless varieties created to lift people's spirits. You may enjoy them without worry.
